Hmm, I could activate Spark Reaper's ability ({3}, sacrifice a creature or planeswalker: gain 1 life and draw a card) to sacrifice it before combat damage. I'd lose Spark Reaper either way — I either sacrifice it and draw a card + gain 1 life, or it dies in combat for nothing. Sacrificing it is strictly better! I have 5 untapped lands (3 Swamps, 2 Forests), so I can pay the {3} cost.

But wait — if I sacrifice it, it's removed from combat, so Berg Strider takes no combat damage. That means the 4/4 stays undamaged. Vs if combat happens, Berg Strider takes 2 damage and Spark Reaper dies. So it's: draw a card and gain 1 life, but opponent's Berg Strider stays at full health. vs. deal 2 damage to Berg Strider but lose Spark Reaper for nothing.

Drawing a card is much more valuable than 2 damage on a creature I probably can't remove anyway. Let me sacrifice Spark Reaper to itself.

llmEvents.reasoning:
Ossuary Rats ETB trigger — 1 damage to target creature. I need to kill Avalanche Caller (1/3)! 1 damage kills a 1/3? No, 1 damage to a 1/3 leaves it at 1/2. It doesn't kill it.

Hmm, then which target is best? Goblin Shortcutter is 2/1 — 1 damage kills it! That removes a 2/1 attacker. Berg Strider (4/4) — 1 damage leaves it at 4/3, irrelevant. Avalanche Caller (1/3) — 1 damage leaves it at 1/2.

Actually, killing Goblin Shortcutter saves me 2 damage per attack and removes the "can't block" ETB threat if they replay it. But Avalanche Caller's ability to animate 4/4 hexproof snow lands is more dangerous long-term.

At 1 life, I need to stop ALL damage. Let me kill Goblin Shortcutter to reduce the number of attackers I need to block next turn.

Good, targeting Goblin Shortcutter with the 1 damage — kills it. Now let me think about what else to do.

I have 3 untapped lands (1 Forest, 2 Swamps) and Crushing Canopy in hand. Crushing Canopy ({2}{G}) can destroy enchantment or flying creature. Nothing useful to target right now.

I could use Portcullis Vine's ability ({2}, {T}, sacrifice defender: draw a card). This costs 2 mana and I sacrifice Portcullis Vine (a defender). But I need Portcullis Vine as a blocker! With it I have 4 potential blockers: Roving Keep, Grave Bramble, Portcullis Vine, and Ossuary Rats (summoning sick but can still block).

Opponent can attack with: Berg Strider (4/4), Avalanche Caller (1/3), plus animated snow lands (4/4 hexproof each, costs {2} per). They have 6 mana and 3 snow lands. They could animate up to 3 snow lands (6 mana = 3x{2}), giving them potentially 5 attackers! But each animated land is also their mana source, so animating 3 means using all their mana.

With Icebind Pillar they can also tap one of my blockers. They need {S} for that.

I need as many blockers as possible. Keep Portcullis Vine. Let me pass to combat.

annotations.description: Kept a 7-card hand with 6 lands and only 1 spell (Spark Reaper). This hand has almost no action and will rely entirely on topdecking to compete. A mulligan to 6 would very likely produce a much better hand with a reasonable spell-to-land ratio.
annotations.actionTaken: Kept a hand with 6 lands and Spark Reaper as the only spell
annotations.betterLine: Mulligan to 6 to find a hand with a better balance of lands and spells

annotations.description: Playing Mountain instead of Snow-Covered Island as the first land. Snow-Covered Island is slightly better because snow mana is more valuable for Icebind Pillar's activated ability and Berg Strider's freeze effect. Either way, Ornery Goblin can be cast on turn 3 by playing Mountain second.
annotations.actionTaken: Played Mountain as first land
annotations.betterLine: Play Snow-Covered Island to get a snow source online sooner, enabling Icebind Pillar's snow-activated ability and Berg Strider's freeze bonus when cast later

annotations.description: Cast Goblin Shortcutter in postcombat main phase, completely wasting its ETB trigger that prevents a creature from blocking this turn. Ornery Goblin was available at the same cost with a persistent combat-relevant ability.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Goblin Shortcutter in postcombat main, wasting its 'can't block this turn' ETB
annotations.betterLine: Cast Ornery Goblin instead, saving Goblin Shortcutter for a precombat main phase where its ETB can enable attacks past a blocker.

annotations.description: Playing a Swamp when a Forest would have been better for mana diversity. The player already has a Swamp on board for the black pip on Spark Reaper, and has 4 Swamps vs 2 Forests in hand. Playing Forest would improve color balance for future draws while still enabling Spark Reaper this turn (Forest + existing Swamp + new Forest = 3 mana including 1B).
annotations.actionTaken: Played Swamp as their land drop
annotations.betterLine: Play Forest to improve mana diversity, since they have 4 Swamps and only 2 Forests in hand, and already have a Swamp on board for black mana needs.

annotations.description: Cast Goblin Instigator before playing a land drop. Should always play the land first to maximize information and flexibility. With the land played first, they'd have 3 mana available and could still cast the same spells, but would retain the option to choose which land to play based on how the spell resolves.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Goblin Instigator with 2 mana available before using the land drop
annotations.betterLine: Play Mountain (or Snow-Covered Island) first, then cast Goblin Instigator. Land-before-spell is correct sequencing when there's no reason to delay the land drop.

annotations.description: Blocking Spark Reaper (2/3) with Goblin Instigator (1/1) at 20 life trades a Goblin body for just 2 damage prevention without killing the attacker. With Muxus in hand, every Goblin on board adds +1/+1 to Muxus when it attacks. Losing a Goblin unnecessarily reduces Muxus's potential impact.
annotations.actionTaken: Blocked Spark Reaper with Goblin Instigator, losing it without killing the attacker to save 2 damage at 20 life
annotations.betterLine: Don't block - take 2 damage at 20 life to preserve the Goblin body for Muxus. If blocking is desired, the Goblin Token is marginally better to sacrifice since it's a token rather than a real card.

annotations.description: Cast Goblin Shortcutter in postcombat main phase, completely wasting its 'target creature can't block this turn' ETB trigger since combat already happened. Additionally, didn't play the Mountain land drop before casting to maximize available mana. Icebind Pillar would have been a stronger play here — it's a repeatable tap effect that synergizes with the two Snow-Covered Islands already in play and provides ongoing board control.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Goblin Shortcutter in postcombat main, wasting its ETB, without playing Mountain first.
annotations.betterLine: Play Mountain first, then cast Icebind Pillar ({2}{U}) to deploy a powerful repeatable tap engine that works with snow lands already in play.

annotations.description: Failed to play Mountain from hand during postcombat main phase. This was a free land drop with no downside. Playing it would bring them to 6 lands, enabling Muxus, Goblin Grandee (4RR) next turn. Without it, Muxus is delayed by at least one turn.
annotations.actionTaken: Timed out and passed without playing the Mountain, missing the land drop entirely.
annotations.betterLine: Play Mountain to reach 6 lands, enabling Muxus next turn which could be game-winning with multiple goblins in the deck.

annotations.description: Playing Swamp instead of Forest when holding 3 Swamps and only 1 Forest in hand. Playing Forest first preserves more mana flexibility for future turns while still enabling Grave Bramble (1GG) this turn. With the Forest play, future Swamp drops give better color balance.
annotations.actionTaken: Played Swamp, going to 2G/3B
annotations.betterLine: Play Forest to go to 3G/2B, preserving flexibility since hand contains 3 more Swamps and only needs future black from existing Swamps on board

annotations.description: GPT5 Teach activated Icebind Pillar's tap ability but targeted their own already-tapped Icebind Pillar instead of the opponent's Spark Reaper. This wastes the activation entirely, accomplishing nothing — tapping an already-tapped permanent they own has zero value.
annotations.actionTaken: Targeted their own Icebind Pillar (already tapped) with Icebind Pillar's tap ability
annotations.betterLine: Target Spark Reaper to tap down the opponent's 2/3 creature, preventing it from blocking or using its sacrifice ability

annotations.description: Activated Avalanche Caller postcombat to make a snow land a temporary 4/4 until end of turn, when Goblin Shortcutter could have been cast instead for a permanent 2/1 Goblin body. The temporary 4/4 provides marginal blocking value for one turn, while the Shortcutter would be a permanent board presence and a Goblin for Muxus synergy.
annotations.actionTaken: Activated Avalanche Caller to animate a snow land as a 4/4 until end of turn postcombat
annotations.betterLine: Cast Goblin Shortcutter for {1}{R} to deploy a permanent 2/1 Goblin creature, building board presence and Muxus synergy

annotations.description: Blocked Spark Reaper with Avalanche Caller (1/3) instead of Goblin Shortcutter (2/1). Avalanche Caller is a key card that turns snow lands into 4/4 hexproof haste attackers, making it far more valuable than the Goblin Shortcutter whose ETB has already been used. Additionally, Goblin Shortcutter would deal 2 damage to Spark Reaper (leaving it at 1 toughness) compared to Avalanche Caller's 1 damage.
annotations.actionTaken: Blocked Spark Reaper with Avalanche Caller, losing the snow-land activation engine
annotations.betterLine: Block with Goblin Shortcutter instead — it's expendable (ETB already used, just a 2/1 body), deals more combat damage to Spark Reaper, and preserves the much more impactful Avalanche Caller

annotations.description: GPT5 Teach timed out and took no action with 5 available mana and strong plays in hand. Berg Strider could have been cast to tap down Grave Bramble (the opponent's main blocker) with snow mana freeze, or Frostpeak Yeti could have added a 3/3 body. Additionally, Avalanche Caller could animate a snow land for a 4/4 hexproof haste attacker. Missing an entire turn of development when they have board presence and the opponent is partially tapped out is devastating.
annotations.actionTaken: Timed out and passed without casting anything or activating any abilities.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Berg Strider (spending Snow-Covered Island for {S}) to tap down Grave Bramble and prevent it from untapping, then attack with available creatures. Alternatively, cast Frostpeak Yeti and use Icebind Pillar to tap Grave Bramble before combat.

annotations.description: Activating Avalanche Caller costs 2 mana, leaving only 3 mana — not enough to cast Berg Strider (5 mana) or Frostpeak Yeti (4 mana). This trades deploying a permanent 4/4 body (Berg Strider) with a powerful ETB tap+freeze effect for a temporary 4/4 attacker that reverts at end of turn and risks losing a land.
annotations.actionTaken: Activated Avalanche Caller to animate a snow land as a temporary 4/4, forgoing casting a permanent creature this turn.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Berg Strider for {4}{U} (spending snow mana for the freeze), getting a permanent 4/4 body and tapping down Grave Bramble or Spark Reaper for potentially two turns, creating much better board presence and tempo.

annotations.description: Berg Strider's ETB trigger should target Spark Reaper instead of Grave Bramble. Grave Bramble has defender and can't attack anyway, so tapping it accomplishes very little. Spark Reaper is already tapped but if snow mana was spent (Berg Strider was cast with Snow-Covered Islands), the 'doesn't untap' clause would keep Spark Reaper locked down for an extra turn, preventing the opponent from using it to block or sacrifice creatures for value. Even without the snow clause, targeting a creature that can actually block or attack is more impactful than tapping a defender.
annotations.actionTaken: Targeted Grave Bramble with Berg Strider's ETB tap ability
annotations.betterLine: Target Spark Reaper to keep it tapped down (especially if snow mana was spent, preventing it from untapping), denying the opponent a blocker and sacrifice outlet

annotations.description: Opponent has no untapped creatures to block (Grave Bramble and Spark Reaper are both tapped). Attacking with only Avalanche Caller (1 power) instead of both Avalanche Caller and Goblin Shortcutter (3 total power) leaves 2 free damage on the table.
annotations.actionTaken: Attacked with only Avalanche Caller for 1 damage.
annotations.betterLine: Attack with all available creatures (Avalanche Caller + Goblin Shortcutter) for 3 damage since the opponent has no untapped blockers.

annotations.description: Opponent has almost no blockers available (only Portcullis Vine 0/3). Attacking with just Avalanche Caller 1/3 instead of all creatures wastes the opportunity to deal 6-7 damage to a 14-life opponent. Berg Strider alone would deal 4 damage unblocked.
annotations.actionTaken: Attacked with only Avalanche Caller 1/3
annotations.betterLine: Attack with all three creatures (Berg Strider 4/4, Goblin Shortcutter 2/1, and Avalanche Caller 1/3) to maximize damage while the opponent's board is mostly tapped down.

annotations.description: Activating Avalanche Caller in postcombat main phase to animate a snow land until end of turn is pointless - combat is already over, so even though the land gets haste, it can't attack. The creature reverts at end of turn, providing no lasting value. This wastes 2 mana that could have been kept open or used more productively.
annotations.actionTaken: Activated Avalanche Caller postcombat to animate a snow land that will revert at end of turn with no combat to use it in.
annotations.betterLine: Play Snow-Covered Island first (free land drop), then cast Frostpeak Yeti ({3}{U}) to develop the board with a 3/3 that threatens unblockable damage next turn against an opponent at 7 life. Save the remaining mana for Icebind Pillar activation if needed.

annotations.description: Activating Avalanche Caller instead of Icebind Pillar when the opponent is at 7 life. Avalanche Caller's activation costs {2}, which would require tapping the untapped Snow-Covered Island (the only available attacker as a 4/4) for mana, and there's no untapped un-animated snow land to target. Meanwhile, Icebind Pillar could tap a blocker (like Grave Bramble) to let the 4/4 Snow-Covered Island attack through for 4 damage.
annotations.actionTaken: Activated Avalanche Caller, likely spending the Snow-Covered Island's mana and losing the 4/4 attacker for no useful effect.
annotations.betterLine: Activate Icebind Pillar (using Snow-Covered Island to pay {S}) to tap Grave Bramble, then attack with the 4/4 Snow-Covered Island for 4 damage, putting opponent to 3 life.

annotations.description: Opponent is at 7 life with only defender creatures (Grave Bramble 3/4, Portcullis Vine 0/3, Roving Keep 5/7) available to block. Attacking with only Avalanche Caller deals just 1 damage when much more pressure could be applied. Berg Strider 4/4 could also attack — it can only be effectively blocked by Roving Keep 5/7. Additionally, GPT5 Teach could animate a Snow-Covered Island into a 4/4 hexproof haste creature and attack with it too, creating more attackers than the opponent has meaningful blockers.
annotations.actionTaken: Attacked with only Avalanche Caller (1/3) for 1 damage.
annotations.betterLine: Activate Avalanche Caller to animate a Snow-Covered Island into a 4/4 hexproof haste, then attack with Berg Strider, Goblin Shortcutter, the animated land, and possibly Avalanche Caller. With 4 attackers vs 3 defenders, at least one significant threat gets through, dealing 4+ damage and putting opponent in critical range.

annotations.description: Opponent is at 1 life and GPT5 Teach timed out, casting nothing in postcombat main with 6 untapped lands and multiple castable threats. Frostpeak Yeti (3/3 that can be made unblockable with snow mana) would guarantee lethal next turn through any blockers. Muxus was also castable at exactly 6 mana and could flood the board with goblins. Even Boggart Brute with menace would add pressure. Doing nothing gives the opponent a free turn to stabilize or find answers.
annotations.actionTaken: Timed out and passed without casting any spells
annotations.betterLine: Cast Frostpeak Yeti (4 mana) to guarantee lethal next turn via its unblockable ability with snow mana, or cast Muxus (6 mana) for massive board presence. Even casting Boggart Brute would be better than nothing.
